chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Muhammad al-Shaybani, from Yunus ibn 'Abdyan, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "O Yunus, convey to 'Atiyyah from me that whoever drinks a gulp of wine, Allah has cursed him, and His angels, and His messengers, and the believers."
If he drinks it until he becomes intoxicated, the spirit of faith is drawn out of his body, and a bad, base, cursed spirit mounts within him.

So when he neglects the prayer, the angels reproach him, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant, you have disbelieved, and the angels have reproached you, and a disgrace awaits you with Me.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "A disgrace, a disgrace, just as the disgrace will be. By Allah, the reprimand of the Majestic for an hour is more severe than the punishment of a thousand years."

He said, then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Cursed, wherever they are found, they are seized and killed with a killing." And he said: "O Yunus, cursed is he who neglects the command of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; if he takes to land, He destroys him with it, and if he takes to sea, He drowns him. He is angry for the anger of the Majestic, Exalted is His Name."
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical consequences of drinking wine and neglecting prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the progressive spiritual decay caused by wine, where a single gulp incurs a universal curse, while intoxication expels the spirit of faith and invites a base spirit. The narration emphasizes the severity of neglecting prayer in this state, highlighting that the reproach of the Divine Majesty ('saw'a') is more acute than a thousand years of punishment. This is contextualized within the broader Shia understanding of khamr as a root cause of spiritual blindness, linking the physical act to the metaphysical state of the soul.
